evidence: Independently read Liu et al (2024) - How AI Processing Delays Foster Creativity.pdf, PDF pp. 6, 8-9. Page 8 reports 20 participants; p. 9, section 6.1, explicitly randomizes the order/combinations of the two AI designs and topics. Page 6, section 5.1.2, describes generation from users' ideas and feedback, with three AI-generated RQs per turn. Page 9, sections 6.2.1 and 6.2.3, confirms participant ratings of selected RQs and system-log counts of generated RQs. Thus the auditor accurately describes the outcome-eligibility uncertainty recorded in forms/c842.json, but it does not invalidate the small randomized-study classification. creativity-codebook.md section 3 separately lists randomized studies below 50 for the screening report and excludes them from the dataset; it does not require every other criterion to be resolved before that size classification. The assembled report, creativity-screening-2026-10-04.md lines 1285-1299, labels this an excluded under-50 study and explicitly calls its scores participant ratings. The introduction says these studies score output; the paper does record output ratings and counts. It does not establish that criterion 3 is met. The form retains criterion_3_outcome_scored_on_output=unclear and core=no; tools/build_report.py lines 110-123 deliberately permits that combination in small. Moving this paper to clarify is a proposed change in category precedence, not a verified factual correction.

Independently read all 10 pages of Sattele and Ortiz (2025) - AI as an element to overcome creative fixation in design teams.pdf. PDF p. 3 (printed 411), sections 3.1 and 3.3, reports 19 students in eight teams. PDF p. 4 (printed 412), section 3.3 and Table 1, explicitly states random assignment of AI tools to teams and identifies their differing configurations. The same page, section 4, explicitly states that two design experts evaluated the final outputs for overall creativity using CAT. The auditor is right that the paper supplies qualitative judgments without numerical creativity scores or an arm-specific creativity comparison; the assembled report already states exactly that in row c898 at line 1305. creativity-codebook.md section 3 requires randomized AI variation and an output-based outcome, but contains no additional requirement that a numerical between-arm result be published to list a study in the excluded under-50 category. The missing contrast prevents extracting an effect from these reported results; it does not refute the documented random assignment, sample size, or expert evaluation. The future controlled study on PDF p. 9 (printed 417) concerns validation of the proposed collaboration model and does not negate the earlier random allocation of AI configurations. forms/c898.json and the report accurately describe the available evidence and exclude the paper from the core.
